span.p: A commit touches that write scope

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Keep fixing

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: This test is wrong

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Accept anyway

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The checkout is the developer's. No edit, stash, reset or commit
there without an explicit click. Harness work stays in its worktrees
and harness branches. harness/integration is never their checkout,
so dirty files on main do not block the merge queue
Nothing they wrote is discarded. A revert is a forward commit
A human-owned worktree is never deleted without asking

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A watcher on the checkout, ignoring dependency and build folders,
plus git status and ref checks
Files no active task touches: say nothing
package.json or the lockfile: offer to include it
A new base commit: a digest item, then a base sync
A branch switch: the status bar updates. The landing target stays
A rebase or merge in progress: landing waits
Edits inside a running worktree: same three choices as an overlap

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What did they touch?

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Overlap

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Include it so workers can use it?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A new base commit is merged into harness/integration
Recheck the changed files. Refresh in-flight tasks whose inputs changed
A conflict with a running task goes to its owner as a normal revision
Their commits are the new truth, and are never rewritten
A force-push rebuilds integration from the new base.
Tasks whose base vanished resume from checkpoints
Deleting a file a finished feature added is reported, and asked about
Fixing an already accepted task is a normal commit, then a recheck

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The worker stops at its next boundary
WIP is a checkpoint. The task becomes human-owned

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The worker continues. On landing, merge with their committed
version and resolve or report the conflicts

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: No change. Do not repeat this notice for this file, this session

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Commit with the developer as author. It becomes base
The integrator reconciles it with open dependency intents

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Workers do not see the new package

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Human-owned. The worker stops. WIP stays on a checkpoint ref
Work in that task's worktree, or in their own checkout
Editing is normal. The harness stays out of the way
I'm done, or a chat message, collects the work
Worktree: the harness commits, developer as author
Own checkout: they pick the commits, prefilled from the scope

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Bring integration onto their branch?
Predict with merge-tree first. Auto-land is off

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Fast-forward or a merge commit, as settings chose

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Git can update and leave those files
Proceed only if auto-land is on. Otherwise ask once

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Never touch the tree

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Wait, and recheck when it finishes

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Explicit click

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Show the diff. Commit with them as author. Then land

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Leave it

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Say that restore may conflict. Run only on this click
Never stash silently

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: They land it themselves

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: I fixed it myself. How did it start?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Suggest: verify it as that task?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The same clean verifier. The same locked checks
The same held-back cases

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Result

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Accepted. Author is the developer. Dependents unlock
The node records acceptedBy human, the commit and the receipt
The office shows the CEO's stamp

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Next

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A product decision. Change the expectation, with an impact preview
Not a quiet edit of the test

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Record the override and the reason
Dependents see a warning. It is in the final summary

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
If an export or a schema changed: compatible is done.
Incompatible consumers are re-briefed, and the preview shows the impact
Files outside the task's scope are listed: record them on their own,
attach them to this task, or leave them unrecorded
After days away, re-entry reconciliation runs before anything starts
